items.note: Association organized at Larrow Green 1889, Gideon Vose first president, creamery built 1891 - all present in narrative 1.
Article VII stated correctly: paid by butterfat test, not milk weight, and the test of the station where he delivers governs.

Does not state inside Section A that the rule is what made a wrong test cost money; only quotes 'the sentence on which the whole trouble turned'. The causal statement appears at B4, and credit does not travel from B-G into A.
Only Hobart Sill (buttermaker) named; Effie Loomis (secretary, minute book) and Wilbur Teague (bookkeeper) absent. Core fact of the officer list not stated.
Selby Vose absent from Section A entirely. Named only at B4, and there with the planted 1911 manager date rather than 1913.
The 'station gain' ledger line appears only at C1(a); credit does not travel from Section C into Section A.
Ostrey Hollow station, seven miles up the valley, opened 4 May 1896, glassware borrowed from Larrow Green (Sill's) for the first season.
No description of how the system worked - no weighing, composite sample, graduated neck, fixed pipette charge, cream shipped / skim returned.
Core fact present: outfit from Ammon & Sons, in use 1 May 1897, correctly defended against the planted 1898 and the 1899 variant. Tarnet and the 14 April 1897 invoice date not given.

Invoice reproduced: six dozen pipettes, twelve dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, total $77.93 (planted $77.39 mentioned only as a within-source discrepancy). Marked capacity 17.6 c.c. never stated.
Flatness of the 0.19 shortfall across months and years is argued only at C1(a); nothing in Section A states it, and 0.19 never appears in Section A.
Nothing about the pipette being uncheckable without a burette, or that no burette existed in the county.

Ansel Keddie, tester at Ostrey Hollow, twenty-nine unbroken seasons from 1896 to 1925. Dismissal date 30 April 1925 appears only at B4, and the span end is given as 1925 rather than 1924, but the core service-and-its-end fact is in Section A.
No bench routine, no test-book columns (date, patron, pounds, test, fat), no crossed-and-initialed corrections.
The summary leaf's 3.80 and 3.61 never appear in Section A; the pair appears only at C1(a). Both figures are required and credit does not travel from Section C.

Nine weeks of 1911, glass broke 8 May, borrowed measure until 10 July, readings rose and fell back the day the station's own glass returned, Keddie's question mark. The 3.80/3.61 figures are not given, but the item's core natural-experiment fact is fully stated.
Orra is named as the tester's wife but never as Orra Brant or as Emmet Brant's sister; at B2 the run explicitly denies the sibling link is established, and at C2 denies Emmet was the largest patron.
The 1919 water circular appears only at B4, not in Section A (Section A has only Grigg's 1919 covering letter). Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement absent entirely.
Death in 1934 under the imputation, impoundment of the test book in 1925, and the 1959 transfer to the county historical rooms all absent.
Answers 'granddaughter' correctly, resting on r22's own dated closing self-correction. No corruption deduction: 'great-niece' is quoted as the corrected error, not asserted.
Derivation not given - never states Ivy is Duncan Keddie's daughter and Duncan is Ansel's son. At B2 it states the opposite, that no source names which of Ansel's children is Ivy's parent.

Does not answer 'second cousins'. Verdict is 'not fully determinable - at best a plausible second cousin'; the chain is laid out conditionally ('if Orra were that same sister... could... come out as') and then disclaimed. This half is not an abstention item, so declining loses the point.

Abstention item A08 unaddressed: the full-vs-half sibling question between Emmet and Orra is never raised, so the run neither declares it unsettleable nor says it does not change the answer. No -2 either, since nothing is asserted about it.

Abstention item A01 not abstained. The verdict sentence is 'no blood or marriage relationship is established anywhere in the notes - only an institutional one', reinforced by 'that silence is meaningful rather than just a gap' and 'not a family one'. That settles the negative pole rather than declaring the sources unable to settle it.

States the opposite of what is established: claims no retelling asserts or implies a Vose-Keddie tie. In fact two narrators assert a cousinship from talk (r01, r21) and one denies it flatly (r18). The run's whole argument rests on a silence that is not there.

Key requires 16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95, i.e. tests read 95 percent of true, short 5 percent, derived from the glassware as the question demands. The run's committed answer is 5.25 percent (the ledger's station-gain note) and its glassware paragraph carries no measurement at all - 16.72 and 17.6 appear nowhere on the sheet.
Key requires $19,000 and 20 percent / one fifth; both required. Run asserts $19,600 and 19.4 percent - exactly the NT-8 cascade - and explicitly rejects its own correct $19,000 cross-check.
Key gives a determinate answer (200,000 x 3.42% = 6,840 lb credited). C2 is not an abstention item anywhere in the key or in batches.md, so 'cannot be determined' scores 0.
Key gives a determinate answer (true test 3.42 / 0.95 = 3.60; 7,200 - 6,840 = 360 lb owed). Not an abstention item; 'cannot be determined' scores 0.
Key gives a determinate answer (360 x $0.24 = $86.40). Not an abstention item; 'cannot be determined' scores 0.

deductions.reason: Corruption: asserts the planted loss of $19,600 as fact at C1(d) - 'the best-attested total value of the shortfall' (F081). True figure $19,000.
Corruption: asserts Selby Vose became manager in 1911 at B4 (catalogued planted error; the key has 1913).

Gullibility: abstention item A01 (B4) answered with a definite verdict - 'no blood or marriage relationship is established... only an institutional one... not a family one', with the silence read as meaningful - rather than a declared inability to settle it.
